title: Stop Evaluating Models Like It's the 50s - Alejandro Vidal, Mindmakers
talk_summary: Alejandro Vidal applies item response theory (IRT) from psychometrics to LLM benchmarking, replacing raw accuracy counts with per-item difficulty (B) and discrimination (A) parameters plus per-model ability (theta). He shows this enables benchmark auditing (finding mislabeled/negative-discrimination items), shrinking benchmarks ~5x while preserving rankings, detecting contamination via residuals, and fingerprinting models.

takeaways.what_they_do: Treat each eval question as an item with a difficulty B and discrimination A estimated across models; items with near-zero or negative discrimination are flagged as noise or mislabeled and audited by an LLM.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can use this to actually find items that are significantly below zero, and we can actually flag them
takeaways.numbers: 97 items vs 484 retained 99% correlation with original ranking (~5x reduction); random subsetting performed far worse

takeaways.technique: Residual/outlier detection to find bad eval items and inconsistent models
takeaways.what_they_do: Compare each model's actual answer to the IRT-predicted probability; large residuals flag either broken items (mislabeled gold answers) or models behaving inconsistently (e.g., bad quantization/inference).
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can actually find out if we are leaking information, if we are overfitting with the benchmark, and other kinds of contaminations

takeaways.technique: Theta-based capability estimation instead of pass-rate
takeaways.what_they_do: Estimate a continuous ability theta per model with a likelihood interval, so two models with near-identical accuracy can be shown to differ by ~1 SD when one solves harder items.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Gemini 3 Pro is by far more intelligent
takeaways.numbers: Claude Opus 4.1: 245 correct vs Gemini 3 Pro: 247 of 337, but ~1 SD apart in theta

takeaways.technique: Adaptive/anchor + fingerprint sets to protect eval integrity
takeaways.what_they_do: Keep a representative anchor set shown to all models plus per-vendor fingerprint sets of hard items; track residuals on fingerprints over time to detect training-on-benchmark contamination.

takeaways.technique: Differential item functioning across model groups
takeaways.what_they_do: Split models into groups (open vs closed weights) and compare per-item curves; items whose curves diverge are biased toward one group.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there are few items that are better for closed weight of models and better for open weights models
